title: Hypnosis Guide Review
intro: This is your whole hypnosis guide, as it is in Git now, with every suggestion from today’s checks marked where it applies. Each colour is one kind of problem (the buttons above say which). Under each marked paragraph is my suggestion: the paragraph as it would read (struck words go, green words come in), why, what stays, and my advice.

Click Approve, Reject or Revise on each card (Revise opens your own version of the paragraph, starting from mine), and add a comment if you want. Nothing counts as approved until you click Approve. Your answers save as you click. Next undecided takes you through them in order.
Some readers’ suggestions I’d leave as they are; they’re hidden unless you tick “The ones a reader flagged and I’d leave” under Filters. Your fix for 15.1 is already in, marked as yours.

edits.before: Deciding to do it . How will you coax yourself to do this? Make it spacious? Make it warm and held? Something else? Preview what you are going to do: will you close your eyes? Will you come out and go back in again? What will you do at the end? If you are going to use a recording, read the script if you can. Know that you can say stop at any time and the induction will end. If you want to change something, say less if you want it to be asking for less from you, or quiet and the talking will stop. You can also just open your eyes and stop, and then come all the way back anyway. You don't need to ask any parts for permission to stop, even if a part tells you that you do.

edits.before: Ending the session . Don’t feel that you have to end the session with a ‘great revelation’! When you have done as much as you want to do, it is a good idea to find out if there is anything that you need to do to make sure that you can leave things where they are for the time being. This might include thanking parts for their help, or making sure that you do something ‘in real life’ (eat a good meal, put a boundary in place, get some rest, repair a relationship, keep a promise etc) or it may be that there is nothing to do!

edits.before: Somatic experiencing: If you would like more information about somatic experiencing, or even a free intro session, please see my somatic guide . In somatic experiencing (SE), you are not thrusting into the trauma. You learn to track. So you might start by tracking, by discovering where the activation is, where a neutral place is, and then whether you can move your attention from one to the other, very slowly, like a snail.

edits.before: Healing the Divided Self , Maggie Phillips and Claire Frederick, (1995) pp 24-27, 45-50, 83-90, covers a lot of aspects of this post, such as interactive hypnosis, helping the subject learn how to learn by using other senses, learning self hypnosis, making sure the subject comes back at the end, etc. However, this is a professional clinical book, not a self help book, so be careful about trying to use the procedures used with the cases, etc in this book for solo work (the same applies to historical information it contains). Also, Adam Eason's work with Benjamin Parris in the International Society of Hypnosis, specifically his article about self hypnosis , should be a useful thing to read (especially the parts that talk about how to learn to learn when you're directing it yourself, and about whether you need another person to help you, and using recordings to help you, etc.)

suggestions.title: Lined up with "Instead of Blame"

edits.before: When you're placing your younger self on trial, how valuable is it to consider how valuable it might have been for them to do what they did at the time, given what they knew at the time? How valuable is it to consider what options they had at the time and how tolerable they were? How valuable is it to consider what the consequences of their actions were at the time? How valuable is it to consider that, even though their actions at the time might have been harmful to you and others, punishing yourself now is not going to give them the capacity they needed at the time and that it's more useful to work on what you can do now to deal with the harm that was caused?
edits.after: When you're placing your younger self on trial, instead of asking which age of you deserves the blame, ask: What was that age of you trying to get, or get away from? What did it understand back then? What options could it actually see? Could it stand to take any of them? What happened because of the choice it made? What was missing? Some ability, or help/protection from someone else? What can you learn or repair now, and how would you act differently in such situations? Even if what it did was harmful to you and others, punishing yourself now is not going to give it the capacity it needed at the time.

suggestions.title: A disclaimer

edits.before: Not everybody has an inner voice , Nedergaard and Lupyan 2024, is not about self hypnosis adaptations, but about people with different amounts of inner speech. suggestions.title: A takeback

edits.before: Chapter 7 of Trauma and Memory , by Peter Levine, 2015, contains useful information on this. This US Veterans Administration website , contains useful general information about hypnosis, such as the fact that it can be very strong and should be carefully used, and that it may result in false memories. This ASCH website , contains information about the usefulness of getting certified in hypnosis, and why it doesn't guarantee competence. Links are available for these and other useful groups in the evidence and specialist sections, but they point to their particular claims, not every use of hypnosis.
